title: 领导力 Day 73：用「四种付费能力」培养下属

questions.question: 一名下属交付稳定不返工；只给问题时，他拿不出多个方案讲清取舍；但他人缘很好，别的团队都爱找他聊。按「四种付费能力」，他该练哪一层？
options: 判断层：执行与人缘都已具备，应当直接批一笔试错资本给他
信任层：已有好人缘这个基础，顺势补上推动多方决策的能力
执行层：方案讲不清说明基本功还不稳，应退回去重练做事标准
专业层：自下而上第一个答「否」的层，人缘好不等于在信任层
questions.explanation: 诊断是自下而上问，第一个答「否」的就是要练的层；而第 3 层看的是有冲突时大家还信不信他，不是人缘。选信任层最诱人，却既跳过了第 2 层，又把一个常见假象当成了真能力。
questions.question_en: A report delivers reliably with no rework; given only a problem, he can't come up with multiple options and explain the trade-offs; but he's very well liked, and other teams love chatting with him. By the "four capabilities people pay for," which layer should he work on?
options_en: Judgment: execution and likability are in place, so approve a sum of trial-and-error capital for him right away
Trust: his popularity is already a foundation, so build on it by adding the ability to drive multi-party decisions
Execution: not being able to explain options means his basics are shaky, so send him back to relearn the standards
Expertise: it's the first layer from the bottom to get a "no," and being well liked doesn't put him on the trust layer
questions.explanation_en: Diagnosis asks from the bottom up, and the first "no" marks the layer to work on; layer 3 is about whether people still trust him when there's a conflict, not about likability. Trust is the most tempting choice, but it both skips layer 2 and mistakes a common illusion for real capability.

questions.question: 下属发现客户在手动导出数据，想试做一个不在计划内的工具。上级回答：「好主意，我来排进下季度的计划。」这句话最大的问题是什么？
options: 没有先让下属做完手上的工作，容易打乱既定的交付节奏
在证据不足时就肯定了想法，应当先要求拿出完整的商业论证
把下属的判断和结果归属都拿走了，TA 练不到为结果负责
排期太慢会错过窗口，这类机会应当立刻投入团队资源去做
questions.explanation: 判断只能在真实的输赢里练出来，「我来排」看似支持，却把这件事变成了上级的决定。正确做法是批一笔输得起的小额资源，一页纸写清赌什么、何时停，项目写 TA 的名字；问题不在速度，也不在证据是否完整。
questions.question_en: A report notices customers manually exporting data and wants to try building a tool that isn't in the plan. The manager replies: "Great idea, I'll put it in next quarter's plan." What is the biggest problem with this reply?
options_en: It didn't have the report finish current work first, which could easily disrupt the planned delivery rhythm
It endorsed the idea before there was enough evidence; a complete business case should have been required first
It takes away the report's ownership of the judgment and the outcome, so they get no practice answering for results
Scheduling this slowly will miss the window; an opportunity like this should get team resources immediately
questions.explanation_en: Judgment can only be built through real wins and losses; "I'll schedule it" looks supportive but turns this into the manager's decision. The right move is to approve a small stake you can afford to lose, have a one-pager spell out what's being bet on and when to stop, and put the report's name on the project; the problem is neither speed nor whether the evidence is complete.

questions.question: 一位已能独立拿方案的后端工程师，第一次接手完全陌生的数据管道任务。按 Grove 的任务相关成熟度，该怎么带？
options: 顺势提到信任层，给舞台和兜底，让 TA 在局里长起来
继续只问思路不给答案，否则会挫伤这位专家的积极性
先等 TA 在原领域升到更高层次，再安排这种陌生任务
这项任务上按较低层带：给标准、做示范，带法按任务定
questions.explanation: 同一个人在不同任务上可能处在不同的层，所以带法按任务定，不按人定。「用教练方式带专家」确实是常见错误，但那是在 TA 已成熟的任务上；到了陌生任务，只问不教反而是放任。
questions.question_en: A backend engineer who can already come up with solutions independently takes on a completely unfamiliar data pipeline task for the first time. By Grove's task-relevant maturity, how should you manage them?
options_en: Move them up to the trust layer: give them a stage and a safety net, and let them grow in the thick of it
Keep asking only about their thinking and give no answers, or you'll dampen this expert's motivation
Wait until they reach a higher layer in their original domain before assigning an unfamiliar task like this
Manage them at a lower layer on this task: set standards and demonstrate; the approach follows the task
questions.explanation_en: The same person can sit on different layers for different tasks, so the approach depends on the task, not the person. "Coaching an expert like a beginner" is indeed a common mistake, but that applies to tasks where they're already mature; on an unfamiliar task, asking without teaching just leaves them to fend for themselves.

title_en: Leadership Day 73: Developing People Through the Four Capabilities People Pay For
